situation:
You are to assume the role of operations manager of CASA ROJA TAQUERIA, a chain of nine quick-serve taco and burrito restaurants. The owner (judge), the third generation of the family to run the company, has asked you to recommend how the lunch rush should be staffed at the two stores losing the most new employees.

Casa Roja Taqueria was opened by the owner's grandmother fifty years ago. New crew members are trained on the line by the one certified trainer each store has. More than half of the people hired this year left within their first thirty days, and most of them said no one had ever explained the job to them.

The lunch rush is where the training breaks down. Between eleven and one, a store can either keep the delivery-app pickup shelf stocked or keep the dine-in counter moving, but the crew is not large enough to do both well. New crew members learn by having directions shouted at them across a hot line, and several have written about those shifts on their personal social accounts. The company's review pages and app listings now carry complaints someone has to answer.

The owner (judge) wants a recommendation. Turning the delivery apps off during the rush would free the trainer to walk each new crew member through the work step by step, but the apps bring in a third of weekday sales and shutting them off fills the listings with complaints from delivery customers. Keeping the apps on protects that revenue, but the counter guests keep waiting and the new hires keep learning by being shouted at, and they keep quitting inside thirty days.

You will present your recommendation to the owner (judge) in the owner's (judge) office. The owner (judge) will begin by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the owner's (judge) questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
